messages.content:
Three independent readers read the same non-disclosure agreement (NDA) and decided whether it supports one statement (the hypothesis). They may agree or disagree, and a program has checked each of their quotes against the document. Your job is to make the final decision yourself, from the document.

<document>
<document 301 omitted, sha256 d6e9f02917bc6f8e>
</document>

<hypothesis>
Confidential Information may include verbally conveyed information.
</hypothesis>

<readings>
<reading id="A">
label: Entailment
confidence: 92
reason: Clause 1.1.2 expressly defines orally imparted information as Confidential Information when the Discloser informed the Recipient it was imparted in confidence, so verbally conveyed information may be Confidential Information.
<quote check="exact">1.1.2 In respect of Information that is imparted orally, any Information that the Discloser or its representatives informed the Recipient at the time of disclosure was imparted in confidence;</quote>
</reading>
<reading id="B">
label: Entailment
confidence: 96
reason: Clause 1.1.2 expressly defines orally imparted information as Confidential Information when it is identified as confidential at the time of disclosure.
<quote check="exact">1.1.2 In respect of Information that is imparted orally, any Information that the Discloser or its representatives informed the Recipient at the time of disclosure was imparted in confidence;</quote>
</reading>
<reading id="C">
label: Entailment
confidence: 95
reason: The definition of Confidential Information expressly covers orally imparted information that the Recipient was told at the time of disclosure was confidential.
<quote check="exact">1.1.2 In respect of Information that is imparted orally, any Information that the Discloser or its representatives informed the Recipient at the time of disclosure was imparted in confidence;</quote>
</reading>
</readings>

The readings are evidence about where to look, not votes: a majority can be wrong, and a quote marked "missing" was not found in the document. Read the relevant parts of the document yourself.

Choose exactly one label:
- Entailment: the document states or clearly implies that the hypothesis is true.
- Contradiction: the document states or clearly implies that the hypothesis is false.
- NotMentioned: the document does not address the hypothesis, or says too little to decide.

Evidence is required. For Entailment or Contradiction, give 1 to 3 quotes copied character for character from the document (no paraphrase, no ellipses), each as short as it can be while still carrying the point. They will be checked against the document. For NotMentioned, give an empty list.

Give a confidence from 0 to 100: your probability, in percent, that your label is correct. Give a one-sentence reason.

Answer only with the JSON object the response format asks for: label, confidence, quotes, reason.

content.text: {"label":"Entailment","confidence":95,"quotes":["1.1.2 In respect of Information that is imparted orally, any Information that the Discloser or its representatives informed the Recipient at the time of disclosure was imparted in confidence;"],"reason":"Clause 1.1.2 expressly includes orally imparted information within Confidential Information when the Recipient is told at disclosure that it is confidential."}
